result.topic_en: A geometric diagram on a lattice of points (marked by crosses and dots) showing a large tilted square subdivided into four quadrants, with red lines forming a triangular/hexagonal partition in one quadrant, plus two small sketches of a lattice square dissected into numbered regions (0, 1, 2, 3), apparently relating to counting lattice points in rotated squares in connection with Gaussian integers.
result.transcription:
[Diagram: a rectangular lattice of points marked alternately by crosses and dots; a large tilted square drawn over it, divided by two lines into four smaller tilted squares; in the upper-left sub-square red lines join marked lattice points, forming triangles; faint pencil lines form a triangular network over the whole figure]

[Small sketch, lower left: a tilted quadrilateral on a few lattice points, divided into regions labelled]
3 \quad 2
0 \quad 1

[Small sketch, lower right: a square dissected by oblique lines into regions labelled]
1 \quad 2 \quad 1
2 \quad 0 \quad 1
1 \quad 1

methods.what: Geometric dissection of a tilted square on the integer lattice into numbered pieces (apparently to compare areas or lattice-point counts of a rotated square, as for Gaussian-integer residues modulo a complex number)
